why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against its expect line. Check 1 passes: its values ('00042', '  ab', 'xxx', '**7') all follow from left padding to width characters, with a space as the default fill. Check 2 passes: every case is s at or above width. Check 4 passes: exit status 0 is left as Advisory, which is looser than the words, not stricter. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition says every exported function "(this must include capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft)" prints HAS-SECTION. The expect line only asks for a section for whatever functions index.js exports. It does not require capitalize, slugify or truncate to stay exported. A PR that dropped one of those exports and still documented every remaining export would meet the words but fail this PASS condition. That fixed list of names is a test the words don't force, so it belongs under Advisory.
